claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

test_case.agent_script:
=== YOUR SITUATION PROFILE ===
You live in the UK.
You are inquiring about your 1 child:
  - Alex is 18 years old and lives with you.

Here are the exact details of your circumstances to use when answering the agent's questions:

Regarding Alex:
  - Claimant lives in the UK
  - Child is 18 and in approved education
  - Child lives with claimant
  - Child is not in local authority care
  - Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation
  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Let me start by asking about your child or children.

**How old is the child you're claiming for?** 

Please tell me:
- The name(s) and age(s) of the child/children you want to claim Child Benefit for

This will help me determine which eligibility rules apply to your situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I'm asking about my son Alex - he's 18 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you're asking about **Alex, who is 18 years old**.

Since Alex is between 16 and 19, I need to check whether he qualifies under the education or training rules. Let me navigate to the next question.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to understand Alex's current situation:

**Is Alex currently in full-time education or training?** 

For example:
- Full-time at school, college, or university
- Full-time vocational training
- Apprenticeship

Or has he **recently left education** (within the last 20 weeks)?

Please let me know which applies to Alex's situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is still in full-time education. He's studying for his A-levels at sixth form college.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is in full-time education studying A-levels at sixth form college. Let me navigate to the next step to validate the education level.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Now let me check the details of Alex's education to ensure it qualifies:

**For Alex's A-level studies at sixth form college, can you confirm:**

1. Is it full-time study (at least 12 hours per week of supervised study)?
2. Is the sixth form college funding this, or is it employer-funded training?
3. Is Alex married?

A-levels are approved education for Child Benefit purposes, so as long as these conditions are met, we should be on track to confirming his eligibility. Once you confirm these details, I can move to the final checks.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, it's definitely full-time - he's there every weekday during term time, so well over 12 hours a week. The sixth form college is funding it, not an employer. And no, Alex isn't married.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex's education clearly qualifies. Let me move to the final eligibility check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now for the penultimate check:

**Does Alex work in paid employment?** 

Specifically:
- Is he working less than 24 hours per week (or not in paid work at all)?

This is important because children aged 16+ working 24 hours or more per week wouldn't qualify for Child Benefit.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't work at all. He's just focusing on his studies at the moment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Alex doesn't work, so that criterion is met. Let me move to the final check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Almost there! Just one more check:

**Is Alex receiving any of the following benefits in his own right:**
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)?
- Universal Credit (as his own claim)?

These would affect his eligibility.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't receive any benefits in his own name. He's still dependent on me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me proceed to the final check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good news! Now I need to ask about apprenticeships:

**Is Alex in an apprenticeship?** 

If yes, which type and in which country (England, Scotland, or Wales)?

Since Alex is in full-time A-level education, I'm expecting he's not in an apprenticeship, but I need to confirm this for the eligibility assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in an apprenticeship. He's just doing his A-levels at sixth form college.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is not in an apprenticeship. Now let me move to check your residency, as this is the final major requirement for Child Benefit eligibility.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Now I need to check your residency status for Child Benefit:

**Which of the following best describes your situation:**

1. **You normally live in the UK** (this is the main route for most people)
2. **You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme**
3. **You have pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme** (if yes, please tell me if you're: working, job-seeking, a student, have sufficient resources, or are a family member of an EEA/Swiss national)
4. **You're a Crown servant living abroad** in certain qualifying countries

For most UK residents, option 1 will apply. Which describes your situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, option 1 - I normally live in the UK.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! You meet the residency requirement. Now let me check the final key criterion - that you have responsibility for Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to confirm that you have responsibility for Alex:

**Which of the following applies to you:**

1. **You live with Alex** (you share a home)
2. **You contribute to Alex's upkeep** (you pay for food, clothes, pocket money, housing, presents, etc. - at least equivalent to the Child Benefit amount)
3. **You pay maintenance** under a court order or agreement towards Alex's care

Which of these applies to your situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Option 1 - Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! You live with Alex, so you have responsibility for him. Let me proceed to the final checks.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check if anyone else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

For example:
- The other parent?
- A grandparent or other relative?
- Anyone else?

If yes, are you and the other claimant in agreement about who should be claiming, or is there a dispute?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex. It's just me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! You're the sole claimant for Alex. Let me proceed to the final location check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Almost done! Just need to confirm where Alex is living:

**Is Alex:**

1. **In hospital** for a long-term stay?
2. **In local authority care** (in a children's home or similar)?
3. **Fostered** by another family?
4. **Living normally** at home with you?

Which applies?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Option 4 - he's living normally at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Let me proceed to the final check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Final question:

**Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words, are you paying for his housing and living costs, or is the council providing support for this?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the council isn't paying anything - I'm covering all his accommodation and living costs myself.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! You've met all the eligibility requirements for Child Benefit for Alex. Let me now provide you with your final outcome.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Now let me record your final outcome:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## **✅ GOOD NEWS - YOU ARE ELIGIBLE FOR CHILD BENEFIT FOR ALEX**

Congratulations! Based on the eligibility assessment, **you qualify for Child Benefit for Alex**.

---

### **Why Alex Qualifies:**

✓ **Age & Education:** Alex is 18 and in full-time approved education (A-levels), studying well over the required 12 hours per week  
✓ **Work Status:** Alex is not working (doesn't exceed 24-hour weekly limit)  
✓ **Benefits Status:** Alex is not receiving ESA or Universal Credit in his own right  
✓ **Apprenticeship:** Alex is not in a disqualifying apprenticeship  
✓ **Residency:** You normally live in the UK  
✓ **Responsibility:** You live with Alex and provide his accommodation and living costs  
✓ **No Other Claimant:** No one else is claiming for Alex  
✓ **Council Support:** The local council is not paying for Alex's accommodation or maintenance  

---

### **Next Steps - How to Claim:**

1. **Apply online** at www.gov.uk/child-benefit or **by post** using form CH2
2. **Provide proof of identity** for yourself and Alex
3. **Provide Alex's birth certificate** or adoption certificate
4. **Be aware of the High Income Child Benefit Charge** - if you or a partner earns over £60,000 per year, you may need to pay back some or all of the benefit through tax

---

### **Payment Details:**

- Child Benefit is normally paid **every 4 weeks** directly to your bank account
- You can request **weekly payments** if you're a single parent or receiving certain other benefits

For more information, visit: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim

**Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?**
